items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes c_1, c_2 and the general Chern polynomial of a derived tensor product E tensor^L F of two perfect objects whose Chern classes are defined, together with the multiplicativity of the Chern character and the binomial formula P_p(E tensor^L F) = sum_{p_1+p_2=p} binom(p, p_1) P_{p_1}(E) P_{p_2}(F) (statement lines 9600-9622). The proof does not simply quote the vector bundle case: after an envelope reduces both objects to locally bounded complexes of finite locally free modules, the author sets up an abstract combinatorial model of a finite set S with a sign map and a function f into a commutative ring, defines P_p(S, f, epsilon) = sum_{s in S} epsilon(s) f(s)^p, and proves the binomial identity there by reducing to the polynomial ring on the disjoint union S amalg S' and comparing the coefficient of every monomial (proof lines 1024-1063 region, that is proof lines 9637-9653). The c_1 formula is then derived exactly from P_1 and r(E) = P_0(E), and the c_2 formula is checked by expanding P_2 in the same splitting-principle style (proof lines 9654-9676). Organising the computation through the polynomials P_p rather than through individual Chern classes is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
